patch.summary: Replaces the areas of an existing token, keeping its bearer value.
patch.description:
## Why this exists, given that it did not

A token used to be born with its areas and keep them until it was revoked, and that was a
real promise: a leaked bearer could never become more dangerous than it was on the day it
leaked. Re-scoping gives that up, and the trade is deliberate. The alternative in practice
was not "narrow tokens forever" — it was a person minting `api:*` up front because
reconnecting every client to widen a token later is expensive, which is a worse outcome for
exactly the same leak. What replaces the old guarantee is the record: issuing, re-scoping
and revoking all write an event, so "when did this token gain that area" has an answer.

Two limits keep the reversal from being a bridge. The areas go through the same
[`resolve_scopes`] the minting path uses, so `capture:*` stays unmintable *and*
ungrantable; and only a token the API token list already shows can be re-scoped at all, so
a browser-capture token cannot be turned into an API token by naming its id here.

post.summary: Renames a package **and the folder its files live in** (RD-106-13).
post.description:
The plain `PATCH /api/v1/packages/{id}` deliberately does not do this: it changes a label,
and a label change must not move data. This does, and is therefore its own request, with
its own refusals.

Two-phase, like a category change: the row is written first — new name, new destination,
the old one kept in `previous_destination`, every stored absolute path rewritten — and the
scheduler then carries the folder over. An interruption between the two leaves the package
pointing at a folder that does not exist yet, which is precisely the state
`relocate_package` is built to finish, on the next pass or after a restart.

**A taken name is refused, not avoided.** Every other path in this codebase reaches for
`rd_files::collision_free_path`, which appends ` (1)` and moves on. That is right when a
file lands somewhere by itself and nobody is watching, and wrong here: somebody typed this
name, and silently storing a different one would leave them looking at a folder they did
not ask for and cannot tell apart from the one they meant.

Pairing request for a machine API token.

Separate from [`CapturePairRequest`] because a capture agent has no scope choice: it
always gets `capture:*`, while an API client picks between full access and read-only.

Legacy: mint `api:read` instead of `api:*`. Superseded by [`Self::scopes`].

call that quietly grants more than it was asked for is the one mistake this whole model
exists to prevent.

intentions. Empty is refused: it has no legacy meaning here, and "no access at all" is
spelled by revoking the token.

AuthProfileSummary.description: The auth profile a replay would use, without any of its secrets.

Normalized domain and path a profile applies to.

The path prefix selects *which* profile matches a URL. It is deliberately **not** a
containment boundary: no HTTP mechanism keeps a credential from travelling to another
path of the same host on a redirect, and cookies do not treat paths as a security
boundary at all. Host containment is real; path containment is not.

passkeys_available.description: Whether a passkey is enrolled, so the sign-in screen knows to offer it.

Automation.description:

Splitting the two is what makes an edit safe while runs are in flight: a run holds the
version it started with, so changing an automation never rewrites the rules a running
attempt is being judged by.

An automation together with the definition currently in force.

Returned as one object because an editor needs both and a second round trip to fetch the
definition of every listed automation is the kind of thing that makes a list page slow.

Record everything present at activation as already seen, and act only on what
appears afterwards.

What the *first* poll of a subscription does with everything already there.

This exists because the alternative is a channel with a decade of uploads arriving in

Which credential the secret slot holds, for a provider that offers a choice. Restoring

vault, and a bundle is a file somebody sends. An import that needs one arrives switched
off, so it cannot poll with no credential and report a failure nobody caused.

What no bundle ever contains, stated so the approval is informed. Codes the client
translates, each with the English the archive keeps (RD-120-15).

One category in a routing bundle. Carries the storage root by name instead of id so the

BundleSubscription.description:
A subscription in a settings bundle (RD-080-07).

The item archive is deliberately absent: history is not configuration, and telling
another machine it has already downloaded things it has not is the one mistake here that
silently loses content. A restored subscription is unprimed and applies its backlog

autoplay.description: Whether the card slider turns its pages on its own (RD-120-37); off when absent.

card_ratio.description:
The shape of a card's image area (RD-120-42). Absent from a bundle written before it

Where an indexer's own categories are routed, and which of them are asked for.

and left it pulling the whole feed. Defaulted, so an older bundle still restores.

every_release.description:
Keep every release of an episode rather than only the first (RD-110-21). Absent from

schedule.description:
The cron expression replacing the interval (RD-130-19). Absent from a bundle written

secret_slot.description: Slot of the indexer API key inside the encrypted section, if the subscription has one.

view.description:
How the LinkGrabber draws the pending hits (RD-120-37). Absent from a bundle written
before it existed, which restores as the list every subscription showed then.

BundledTool.description: A helper program the packages ship in `vendor/`, with the licence it ships under.

file.description: Where the full text lies in an installed package.

license.description: SPDX expression; `LicenseRef-…` where the licence has no SPDX identifier.

CandidateAuthProfileMode.description: The three ways a link can choose a profile.

CandidateAuthProfileRequest.description:
Which cookie/authentication profile a link should be queued with (RD-080-04).

Mirrors `AuthProfileSelection`'s three states rather than a nullable id, because
"let the scope decide" and "deliberately send nothing" are different intents.

oneOf.description: Required for `pinned`, ignored otherwise.

CandidateCheckRequest.description: Links to check; empty = every open link.

CandidateMirror.description:
One candidate's membership in a mirror group.

A mirror is deliberately **not** a duplicate: [`LinkCandidateState::Duplicate`] means the
very same address is already in the collector and the copy adds nothing, while a mirror is
a *different* address for the same bytes and is kept precisely because it is needed the
moment the chosen one goes offline. Nothing here reads or writes that state, and two links
with the same address are never mirrors of each other.

group.description:
Key shared by the members of the group. Unique within the package and nowhere else:
a group lives inside one package, because that is the unit the queue downloads.

language.description: The language of this mirror, on the same terms as [`Self::quality`].

pinned.description:
Whether a person chose this member by hand (RD-110-19).

A pin outranks [`MirrorPreference`] and survives a regroup: a standing preference is a
default, and a default that silently revises a decision somebody already made is worse
than no default at all. At most one member of a group carries it.

quality.description: The quality of this mirror, as the source named it or as its release name spells it.

selected.description:
Whether this is the member the package would use. Exactly one member of a group
carries it.

media_variant.description: Switches the media variant (`best`, `1080p`, `audio_mp3`, …) of a media link.

Capability.description:
What a tool version can take away.

One variant per gate that actually exists in the code, so a rule cannot promise a block
that nothing enforces.

CapacityShortfallResponse.description: Why a target is holding back work; all four numbers are shown verbatim in the UI.

size_known.description: `false` when no runner could state a size and the headroom policy was applied.

api_key.description:
The key to ask with. Used for this one request and then dropped: nothing is stored, and
a subscription only gains a key when it is saved.

url.description: The indexer's address, as it would be stored on the subscription.

CaptchaAnswerers.description: What the web interface may say about the ways a widget captcha can be answered.

browser_extension_connected.description: Whether that was recent enough to expect the extension to pick up a new challenge.

browser_extension_seen_at.description: When a browser extension last asked for the waiting widgets; absent until one has.

CaptchaConfigResponse.description: Solver configuration as exposed by the API; the API key itself is never returned.

CaptchaKind.description: Which kind of challenge is waiting, for the UI.

CaptchaSolverTestResponse.description: Proof that the solver service answered and accepted the key.

balance.description: Credit left on the account, as reported by the service.

CaptureBrowserSession.description:
A waiting handover as the extension sees it: what it needs to ask the person, and nothing
else. The scope is the service's, never the page's — the extension reads exactly this.

account_label.description: Which account the session is for, so the person can tell two requests apart.

provider_name.description: The provider's display name, for the question the popup asks.

scope.description: The provider's `cookie_scope`: an `https` URL whose host is the only one read.

CaptureCaptchaClient.description:
Which kind of client is polling the waiting widgets.

The desktop agent and the browser extension read the same list with the same kind of
token; the extension names itself so the web interface can tell a person whether one is
connected (RD-108-02). Not naming oneself is allowed and changes nothing — an agent older
than this parameter keeps working.

CaptureCookiesRequest.description: Cookies handed over by a capture client for one approved domain.

CaptureFileKind.description: What the file was taken as.

CaptureFileRequest.description:
A file handed over as JSON: either its bytes or its address, never both.

No `Debug`: the cookies are the one thing in this service's request bodies that must never
reach a log line, and a derived `Debug` is how a body ends up in one.

content.description:
The file's bytes as the browser received them, base64 with the standard alphabet. At
most 48 MiB once decoded.

cookies.description:
The cookies the browser would send to `url`, in the form `capture/cookies` takes: a
Netscape cookie file, or a `Cookie` header. A cookie the browser would not send to `url`
refuses the request. They travel only to that address's own scheme, host and port, and
are never stored. Only with `url`.

file_name.description: The file's name, as the browser would save it.

referrer.description: The page the download started from, sent as `Referer`. Only with `url`.

url.description: The address to fetch once, when the browser could not copy the bytes. http or https.

user_agent.description: The browser's user agent, which some sites bind a session to. Only with `url`.

nzb_imports.description: The NZB imports, one per NZB; empty for a torrent.

oneOf.description: The LinkGrabber intake a torrent became; absent otherwise.

CaptureLinkRequest.description: One structured link of a capture batch, optionally with the request that produced it.

oneOf.description: Metadata to reproduce the GET; sanitized and allowlisted on arrival.

CapturePairRequest.description: Human label for a newly paired native capture agent.

CapturePairResponse.description: One-time bearer plus its revocable metadata.

CaptureSummaryResponse.description:
Figures only, for the desktop tray.

Deliberately not `DownloadSummaryResponse`: that one carries storage entries with their
paths, and this is served to the capture agent, whose token is scoped for handing links in.
The event stream is filtered to intake for the same reason — the full bus would carry
download paths and account names. Counts and byte totals say enough for an icon and a
tooltip and say nothing about what is being downloaded.

bytes_per_second.description:
The queue's smoothed transfer rate, in bytes per second.

Served here so the tray shows the same figure as the web interface. The agent used to
derive its own from two consecutive reads, unsmoothed, which meant two different
answers to the same question; the service keeps the rate now (RD-104-02).

committed_bytes.description: Bytes committed across everything not finished, and the total where it is known.

eta_seconds.description:
Seconds until the queue is through at that rate, or `null` when no honest figure
exists: an entry still to be fetched whose size is unknown, a rate of zero, a paused
transfer. The same rule the web interface follows, because it is the same number.

Taken from the very `queue_rate()` value the rate above comes from (RD-108-01). The
estimate was already being computed there and then dropped, so the tray had the rate
but not the time it implies; a second formula here would have been a second answer to
one question, which is the mistake RD-104-02 exists to have ended.

CaptureToken.description: Revocable token metadata; the bearer secret is never persisted in plaintext.

last_used_at.description:
When the token was last accepted on a request, to the nearest minute.

`None` means it has not been used since it was issued — which is the one thing worth
knowing about a machine token nobody can remember handing out. Coarse on purpose: the
write is throttled, because the alternative is one database write per request for a
field nobody reads in real time.

CapturedBody.description:
Metadata of a captured request body.

Carries no secret reference and no values: the ciphertext reference lives in a SQL
column so it can never be serialized, and only field *names* are kept for the preview.

byte_len.description: Length of the decoded body in bytes.

field_names.description: Form field names only, capped at [`MAX_BODY_FIELD_NAMES`].

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the decoded bytes; consent identity and change detection.

stored.description:
Whether the body was actually stored. `false` when it was refused (too large, a file
upload); the metadata is kept anyway so the UI can explain the block.

CapturedHeader.description: One allowlisted request header captured with a browser download.

CapturedRequest.description:
Metadata needed to reproduce the GET of an intercepted browser download.

Credential-free by contract: cookies, `Authorization` and reusable sessions
are modelled separately (auth profiles), never here.

approved_origins.description: Origins this request may be replayed against. Server-derived.

oneOf.description: Why it cannot be, when `replayable` is false. Server-derived.
Metadata of the request body. Field names only; values live in the secret store.

effective_url.description: Final URL after redirects; only set when it differs from the link URL.

expires_at.description: Deadline read out of the signed URL. Server-derived; a client value is ignored.

has_file_upload.description:
Client's declaration that the request carried a file part. Never trusted for
anything except refusing the body.

method.description: HTTP method; contract v1 accepts `GET`, v2 also accepts `POST`.

replayable.description: Whether the capture can be reproduced at all. Server-derived.

cleanup_extensions.description:
Extensions (without dot) removed after unpacking packages in this category;
`None` = use the global cleanup list.

delete_par2.description:
Whether packages in this category discard the PAR2 recovery set after a successful
unpack; `None` = global default.

plugin_steps.description:
Post-processing plugin steps for packages in this category, by plugin id and in the
order they run; `None` = the global list. An empty list means "none here", which is
how a category switches a globally enabled step off.

recursive_unpack.description: Whether packages in this category unpack nested archives recursively; `None` = global default.

safe_postproc.description:
Whether a failed verification blocks unpacking for packages in this category;
`None` = global default (RD-104-04).

script.description: Default post-processing script for packages in this category.

oneOf.description:
Seeding override for torrents in this category; every unset field inherits from
the global settings.

sfv_verify.description: Whether packages in this category verify `.sfv` checksums; `None` = global default.

upload_enabled.description: Whether packages in this category upload to rclone; `None` = global default.

upload_remote.description: rclone target override in `remote:path` form; `None` = the global remote.

and reorder; the lookup builds a map from it when it needs one.

category_id.description: Where releases in it should go.

source_category.description: The indexer's own category id, e.g. `5040`.

delete_par2.description:
Whether packages of this category discard the PAR2 recovery set after a successful

plugin_steps.description:
Post-processing plugin steps for this category, by plugin id and in the order they

it — not of the rendering, which the interface may have scaled.

Addresses the folder crawlers and site rules handed back for this intake, before any

package. What the LinkGrabber sends while a filter hides part of a package — absent, a

password.description: Archive password; readable again on the package (RD-104-04).

format.description: Which format the upload turned out to be.

The file's bytes, base64 with the standard alphabet. Padding is optional and line breaks

The file's name, as a browser upload would carry it. `/api/v1/containers/import` reads
the format from its extension, and a `{{password}}` marker in it names the archive
password, as it does for a dropped file.

`dlc`, `ccf`, `rsdf` or `txt`, overriding the extension. Read by

Which credential `secret` holds, for a provider that offers a choice. Required for

Reusable per-domain session or authentication profile. Credential fields are write-only

no endpoint ever returns them or their `vault://` reference.

Which of a provider's credential modes an account uses.

Only meaningful for [`CredentialKind::LoginOrApiKey`]; every other kind has exactly one way
to hold an account and stores `None`.

The cookies the extension read for a waiting request, in Netscape format.

delivery per matching rule even if the worker restarts mid-flight.

follows, so what a plugin said stays distinguishable from what the core resolved.

finishes, which leaves them where they are, or gives up, which promotes one of them.

PAR2 repair data rather than payload, decided when the NZB is queued.

A recovery volume that never arrives is not automatically a defect: as long as the
payload is complete, nobody asked for it. Until RD-107-10 the difference existed only

Stored login for `kind == ftp | sftp`; `None` matches the URL against the remote
credential store by host and port when the transfer starts.

DownloadKind.description:
Transport family of a package/file: direct HTTP (incl. hoster resolvers), Usenet or
media fetched through an external extractor (yt-dlp).

DownloadPackage.description: A logical package grouping one or more files.

completed_at.description:
When the package reached `Completed`, for the automatic removal of finished packages.

Distinct from the row's last write: editing a finished package must not look like it
finished again.

enrichment.description:
Fields enrichers contributed to the links this package was built from (RD-107-02).

The union of its files' fields, carried across the enqueue. Without it a rating an
enricher looked up was visible only while the link sat in the LinkGrabber, which for
an auto-queueing subscription is a few seconds.

oneOf.description:
Outcome of the unpack stage of the last post-processing run; `None` when nothing
was extracted.

has_password.description: Whether an archive password is stored.

oneOf.description: Backing NZB import for Usenet packages.

password.description:
The stored archive password, in clear.

Deliberately readable (RD-104-04): an archive password comes from the release title,
the `{{password}}` marker of a file name or the feed, so it is public already, and a
person who wants to unpack by hand — or to understand why an unpack failed — needs it.
This is the *only* secret rDownloader hands back: account passwords, API keys and NNTP
or proxy credentials live in `rd-secrets` and stay write-only.

position.description: Manual queue position inside the same priority (lower runs first).

oneOf.description: Explicit post-processing level; `None` inherits category/default.

script.description: Post-processing script file name (inside the scripts directory); `None` inherits.

DownloadPriority.description: Queue priority of a package; higher priorities are scheduled first.

DownloadRateEntry.description: One entry's live rate and the remaining time it implies.

eta_seconds.description: `None` when the size is unknown or the entry is not moving.

DownloadRatesResponse.description:
Live transfer rates: the queue as a whole, and every entry that is moving.

Entries at rest are left out — their rate is zero and their remaining time is nothing, and
saying so for every finished download in a long list is pure payload.

eta_seconds.description: Seconds until the queue is through, or `None` when no honest figure exists.

oneOf.description:
Bytes still to fetch across queued, retrying, resolving and downloading entries;
`None` while one of them has no known size.

DownloadRenameRequest.description: New file name for a queued, paused or failed download.

DownloadReorderRequest.description: Complete file order of one package; the ids have to be exactly its files, each once.

DownloadResetRequest.description: Options for resetting a single file.

delete_completed_files.description:
Delete a finished payload as well. Off by default: a reset that keeps the file lets the
fresh attempt land beside it instead of destroying the only copy.

DownloadSummaryResponse.description: Aggregated queue counters shown below the download list.

bytes_per_second.description: Combined smoothed transfer rate of the whole queue, in bytes per second.

eta_seconds.description:
Seconds until the queue is through, at the current rate.

`None` whenever a number would be invented rather than measured: nothing is moving, or
one of the entries still to be fetched has no known size, which would make the figure a
lower bound presented as an answer.

remaining_bytes.description:
Everything not yet fetched, including entries that are paused, blocked or already
downloaded and now being verified, repaired, unpacked or seeded.

Deliberately wider than `transferring_remaining_bytes`: this is "how much is still
outstanding", not "how much is on its way". The remaining time is built from the
narrower figure, and the interface names the difference rather than blurring it.

oneOf.description:
Bytes still to fetch across the entries that are actually going to be fetched at the
current rate — queued, waiting to retry, resolving or downloading.

`None` while one of those entries has no known size, because the sum would then be a
lower bound rather than the remainder.

DryRunMatch.description: What a dry run found for one automation.

condition_matches.description: Whether its condition holds for the sample package.

trigger_matches.description: Whether this automation listens for the trigger that was tried.

oneOf.description:
A real package to judge the condition against; `None` evaluates against nothing,
which is what a condition-free automation is.

DynamicRange.description: High dynamic range signalling as reported by the extractor.

EffectiveSeedingPolicy.description: The resolved policy applied to one torrent, with the origin of every field.

The source URL carries a signature or token, so it is not written into the file.
ffmpeg is needed to write tags or cut segments and is not available.
Removing segments re-encodes the media; marking them does not.

EmbedWarning.description: Something an embed policy asks for that cannot be delivered as stated.

EnrichmentField.description: One field an enricher plugin contributed to a link.

fetched_at.description: When it was looked up, so a stale value is recognisable as one.

plugin_id.description:
Which plugin said so. Shown next to the value: a field whose source is invisible is
indistinguishable from something the application knows itself.

ErrorBody.description: JSON body of every REST error.

params.description: Flat parameters referenced by the translated text.

ExpectedChecksum.description: Checksum expected from metadata or the user.

ExtractionResult.description:
Persisted outcome of the unpack stage, kept after the pipeline finished so the UI can
show whether a package was extracted. `None` on the package means nothing was unpacked
(no archives, or the level does not unpack).

Failure.description:
Structured failure with a redaction-safe English message and an optional stable
code (`<domain>.<subject>_<condition>`) that clients translate.

oneOf.description:
This IP may not start another free download from the hoster yet. Retryable, but the
scheduler additionally holds back every other link of the same hoster until it
expires instead of burning waits and captchas on them.

A captcha answer was rejected by the hoster; worth one more attempt with a fresh
challenge, unlike [`Self::NeedsCaptcha`], which means none could be obtained.

FailureKind.description: Stable error classes shared by scheduler, plugins and API.

Field.description:
A field of the event an automation can look at.

Deliberately small and flat. Everything here is either already on the event or cheap to
look up once per run; nothing invites the engine to go and fetch more of the domain
while a condition is being evaluated.

FilterReason.description:
Why an item was not accepted.

A variant per rule rather than a message, so the UI can translate the reason and a test
can assert on it.

GrabberEntryKind.description:
Which table a LinkGrabber entry belongs to.

The list shows two kinds of row in one manual order, and an id alone does not say which: both
are UUIDs, and a collector package id would silently match nothing in `nzb_imports` (and the
other way round), producing an order that writes positions for rows nobody named.

GrabberEntryRef.description: One entry of the LinkGrabber's single manual order.

id.description: The row's id; which table it belongs to is [`Self::kind`], never guessed from the value.

GrabberEntryReorderRequest.description:
A slice of the LinkGrabber's manual order over both kinds of entry, in display order.

A list may be partial - the client sends the rows it is showing, and filters hide rows - but
every entry has to name a row that exists under the kind it claims.

oneOf.description:
The entry the listed ones are placed behind; absent means the head of the list.

Without it a partial list can only describe a prefix, so a drag deep into a long list has
to send everything above it and runs into the bulk bound. The anchor is what keeps a drag
at index 700 the same two entries as a drag at index 2.

HotFolderExecutor.description: Location responsible for watching a hotfolder.

ImportAreaSummary.description:
What an import did, per area. Skipped covers both "already there" and "could not be
resolved"; the counts are what tells somebody the file was not what they expected.

ImportMode.description: Whether an intake source waits for review or directly enters the queue.

ImportSiteRulesResponse.description: The result of an import: every rule, and how many were stored switched off.

signed.description: Whether the file was the signed one and its signature held.

ImportedSiteRuleResponse.description: What became of one rule in an import.

code.description: Why it was refused, as a stable code.

id.description: The rule's id, or the empty string when the body carries none this build can read.

IncompatiblePluginResponse.description: An installed package this build refuses to run.

code.description:
Stable code the UI translates: `plugin.manifest_outdated`,
`plugin.capability_unknown` or `plugin.manifest_unreadable`.

id.description: Plugin id, or the directory name when the manifest cannot say.

IndexerCaps.description: What an indexer says it can do.

limit_max.description: Largest `limit` the indexer accepts, when it states one.

searching.description: Search types the indexer answers, e.g. `search`, `tv-search`, `movie-search`.

server.description: Server name, when it gives one.

IndexerCategory.description: One category an indexer files releases under.

id.description:
The numeric id used in `cat=`; a string because it is an opaque token, not a number
we do arithmetic on.

parent_id.description: Id of the parent category for a subcategory; `None` for a top-level one.

IngressSource.description: Origin of a batch submitted to the LinkGrabber.

InstalledPluginResponse.description:
Redaction-safe metadata for one installed resolver version.

`name` and `description` are the manifest's own values; the plugin manager overlays the
localised ones from `/api/v1/plugins/i18n/{locale}` when they exist.

active.description:
Whether this is the version that wins among the installed ones for its id.

Installing never removes an older version, so two can sit side by side; the highest
SemVer is the one loaded. That rule was never wrong, only invisible — the manager listed
both with nothing to separate them, so the leftover looked like a second, equal plugin.

Says nothing about whether the plugin is switched on; that is a separate choice and
applies to every version of an id at once.

api_version.description: `rdownloader:plugin` WIT version the package was built against.

capabilities.description: Every grant the manifest asks for, as the plugin manager lists them.

execution_count.description:
How many invocations this plugin id has recorded, capped at what the store keeps.

Only the number, never an entry: the manager offers its diagnostics accordion when this
is greater than zero and fetches the entries themselves when somebody opens it, which is
what keeps diagnostics nobody looks at free. Without it the accordion was a button with
nothing behind it, and the panel it opened could not say whether the plugin had never
run or run without incident.

Counted per id, so every installed version of one id reports the same number — the
store records the version in the entry, not in its key.

plugin_type.description: What the plugin is: `resolver`, `transfer`, or whatever an unknown package claims.

digest.description: SHA-256 over the entries' ids, paths and kinds; the approval quotes it back.

excluded.description: What no bundle ever contains, stated so the approval is informed.

InventoryEntry.description: One file the bundle may contain, as the preview shows it.

description.description: What the entry holds, in one sentence, as a code the interface translates.

id.description: The stable id a person selects by.

items.description: How many items it holds right now: plugins, checks, records, fields.

redactions.description: What was removed or replaced before the entry was written.

oneOf.description: One transport (HTTP, Usenet, torrent, media, gallery, stream).

value.description: One transport (HTTP, Usenet, torrent, media, gallery, stream).

oneOf.description: One normalised host, without `www.`.
One provider account.
One category, and therefore everything routed into it.

value.description: One category, and therefore everything routed into it.

LimitScope.description: A scope a profile can put its own limit on, next to the global one.

LimitSource.description: Where a binding limit came from. Ordered from broadest to narrowest.

LinkCandidate.description: An analyzed link awaiting review or enqueue.

auth_profile.description:
Cookie/authentication profile this link is queued with (RD-080-04).

Chosen before queueing so the first attempt at a private page already carries the
right session, instead of failing once and being corrected afterwards. Defaults to
[`crate::AuthProfileSelection::Auto`], which is what every link did before.

cached_at.description:
When a provider last said it holds this file in its own cache (RD-120-36).

Set only by a check that answered [`LinkStatus::Cached`], and cleared by every check
that did not, so it is always the time of the latest check. A cache
changes without telling anybody, so the interface shows the time with it and treats the
value as a measurement, never as a promise. The candidate's state stays `Online`.

cached_by.description:
Which provider gave the cache answer `cached_at` records, by its slug (RD-130-11).

Set and cleared together with `cached_at`, never without it. `None` next to a time is
an answer stamped before the column existed, and the interface then names nobody
rather than guessing.

checked_at.description: When the last online check finished.

created_at.description: When the link was added to the collector.

enrichment.description:
Fields an enricher plugin added (RD-090-14).

Beside the core fields, never merged into them: what a plugin contributed stays
distinguishable from what the application resolved itself, so it can be shown with its
source and so a core field can never be quietly replaced.

error_code.description:
Stable code for `error`, translated by the interface as `server.codes.<code>`.

The text stays beside it as the English fallback, for a row written before the code
existed and for a message a plugin worded itself. A candidate that carries no code
reaches the reader as that text, exactly as every candidate used to.

file_name_declared.description:
Whether `file_name` came from the source rather than from the link's address.

Intake substitutes the address's last segment when the source names none, and the two
look alike afterwards; only this says which it was.

oneOf.description:
Bounded remote-directory summary for `ftp`/`sftp`/`webdav` links; the full listing
is fetched per candidate for the same reason as the torrent file tree.
Extractor metadata and variant choice for media links.

Which mirror group this link belongs to, if any (RD-110-18).

`None` is the ordinary case: a link nothing else points at the same file with is a
download, not a mirror of anything. See [`CandidateMirror`] for why this is separate
from [`LinkCandidateState::Duplicate`].
LinkGrabber package the link is grouped into.

Stored login the online check used to reach the server; carried to the queue row so
the transfer authenticates the same way the probe did.

Consent a person gave for replaying this request, if any.

The encrypted body's `vault://` reference deliberately has **no** field here: it
lives only in `link_candidates.replay_body_ref`, so it cannot be serialized into a
REST or SSE payload by widening this struct.
Request metadata of an intercepted browser download; `None` for every other source.

secret_fragment.description:
Whether the vault holds the fragment this link's address arrived with (RD-110-38).

A flag, not the reference and never the fragment itself. The `vault://` reference
lives only in `link_candidates.secret_fragment_ref`, for the same reason
`replay_body_ref` does: a column cannot be serialized into a REST or SSE payload by
somebody widening this struct. What a reader is entitled to know is that a key is
being kept for this link, and that is exactly what this says.

oneOf.description:
Bounded torrent summary; the full file tree is fetched per candidate so a list
response never carries thousands of entries.

LinkCheckResult.description: Result of probing one link without downloading it.

oneOf.description: Media metadata when the link was probed by the media provider.

LinkStatus.description: Availability reported by an online check.

LogLevel.description: The severity of one stored log record, in `tracing`'s order.

LogRecordResponse.description: One stored record, as the layer redacted it.

LogRecordsResponse.description: A page of the log store, newest first.

captured.description: Records the capture layer handed over since the process started.

dropped.description: Records the capture layer dropped because the sink was behind.

full_page.description: True when the page is full, so a client knows there may be more behind `before_id`.

total.description: Records the whole store holds, whatever the filter.

code.description:
A code from an authenticator app, or a recovery code.

Optional so the first request can omit it: the client learns that a second factor is
required from the `auth.mfa_required` refusal, rather than having to ask in advance
whether this installation uses one. Asking in advance would tell an unauthenticated
caller something about the account.

ManagedToolInfo.description: One managed external tool: what is installed, what is active, what is on offer.

active_path.description: The executable that version points at.

active_version.description: The version the managed stage of the tool lookup answers with.

available_version.description:
The newest version the signed manifest offers for this platform and this application
version, or `null` when it offers none.

can_roll_back.description: Whether a rollback has an earlier installed version to return to.

installed_versions.description: Every version in the store, newest install first.

ManagedToolVersionRequest.description: Which version to install or activate. `null` takes the newest the manifest offers.

ManagedToolsResponse.description: The managed tool store as a whole.

enabled.description: Whether this installation may install and activate tool versions at all.

manifest_issued_at.description: When the publisher signed that manifest.

manifest_sequence.description:
The sequence of the manifest currently in force. `0` is the manifest compiled into
this build, before any refresh.

manifest_url.description: The configured manifest URL, if any.

platform.description: The target triple manifest entries are matched against.

Manifest.description: `manifest.json`: what the archive holds and what was left out.

excluded.description: What no bundle ever contains, in English, for the same reason.

redactions.description: `<path>: <what was redacted>`, in English, for the same reason.

ManifestEntry.description: One file as it was written.

description.description:
What the file holds, in English: this manifest is read outside the application, by
somebody who has no interface to translate a code for them.

oneOf.description: ffmpeg is missing or incomplete, so only progressive formats are usable.
The chosen codec cannot live in the chosen container.
The target container cannot hold what was asked of it.
The inventory was cut at [`super::MAX_MEDIA_FORMATS`].

MediaCompatibilityWarning.description: Something the user asked for that the result does not honour.

MediaEmbedPolicy.description: What to write into the finished file.

info_json.description: The extractor's full info JSON, which carries the description and the source URL.

metadata.description: Title, uploader, date and the rest of the tag set.

thumbnail.description: Cover image from the page's thumbnail.

MediaFormat.description: One normalised entry of the extractor's format list.

format_id.description:
The extractor's own id. Volatile — shown to the user and offered as a pin, but never
the thing a selection is stored as.

format_note.description: The extractor's free-text note (`1080p60 HDR`), display only.

language.description: Lowercased language tag as reported (`de`, `en-US`); `None` when the site says nothing.

video_codec_raw.description: The codec string as reported, kept for display and diagnostics.

MediaFormatCriteria.description:
The persisted selection. Every field is optional or empty-as-any, so an older blob
deserialises into "no opinion" rather than into a filter nobody asked for.

allow_merge.description:
Whether a separate video and audio stream may be merged. Forced off when ffmpeg is
missing, which is what leaves a muxed-only fallback.

audio_languages.description:
Preferred audio languages, best first. A list rather than a single value because
multiple audio tracks (RD-080-02) extend exactly this field.

oneOf.description:
What to write into the finished file and what to cut out of it (RD-080-03).
Always serialised, for the same reason as `tracks`.

output_template.description:
Output template for this job (RD-080-05); `None` uses the configured default.

Neither validated nor expanded here: the evaluator lives in `rd-files`, beside the
sanitiser it depends on, and `rd-files` depends on this crate. The API layer runs
`rd_files::validate` before storing, and the runner falls back to the plain file name
if a stored template turns out not to expand.

preset.description:
The preset these criteria came from (`best`, `1080p`, `audio_mp3`), or `None` for a
hand-built selection. Display only — the criteria are the contract.

oneOf.description:
Extra audio tracks and subtitles (RD-080-02). Empty for a plain download.

Always serialised, unlike the optional fields around it: the generated client type
declares it required, and omitting it would hand the UI an `undefined` to trip over.

MediaFormatInventory.description: The formats one probe found, plus whether the list had to be cut.

truncated.description: `true` when the page offered more than [`MAX_MEDIA_FORMATS`].

MediaFormatKind.description:
Whether a format carries video, audio, or both.

[`MediaFormatKind::Muxed`] is the distinction the whole no-ffmpeg path rests on: a
muxed format is downloadable on its own, a `Video`/`Audio` pair is not.

MediaFormatsResponse.description: The full inventory behind one media candidate, fetched only when the selector is opened.

criteria.description: The criteria currently stored for this candidate.

oneOf.description: What those criteria resolve to right now.

subtitles.description: Subtitle tracks the page offers, manual and automatic kept apart (RD-080-02).

unresolved_code.description:
Why `resolved` is empty, as the resolver's stable code (`media.formats_missing`,
`media.audio_missing`, `media.merge_unavailable`, `media.criteria_unsatisfiable`),
so the selector names the actual reason rather than guessing one (RD-120-50).

MediaInfo.description:
Metadata of one media page as reported by the extractor.

`upload_date`, `extractor` and `video_id` fall out of the same `yt-dlp -J` call as the
rest and are the fields output templates (RD-080-05) are written against.

selected.description: Id of the selected variant (defaults to the configured preference).

upload_date.description: Upload date as `YYYYMMDD`, exactly as the extractor reports it.

video_id.description: The site's own id for the item.

MediaKind.description: Whether a variant produces a video container or an audio-only file.

oneOf.description: Keep whatever the chosen format(s) produce.
Merge/remux into a fixed container without re-encoding.
Extract the audio track into `codec` (`mp3`, `m4a`, `opus`, `flac`).

MediaOutput.description: What happens to the streams once they are fetched.

MediaOutputPreviewRequest.description: A template to preview against one candidate's real metadata.

template.description: The template to expand. Empty previews the plain file name.

MediaOutputPreviewResponse.description: What a template expands to for one candidate.

fields.description: The fields a template may reference, so the UI never has to hard-code them.

relative_path.description: The path relative to the package directory, using `/` separators.

MediaResolutionResponse.description: What a set of criteria resolves to.

embed_warnings.description:
What the embed policy cannot honour (RD-080-03), including a source URL withheld
because it carries a signature.

format_expression.description: The yt-dlp expression that would be used. Diagnostic only.

label.description: Human-readable description of the chosen format (`AV1 1080p60 HDR`).

matched_counts.description:
How many formats each criterion would keep on its own — what makes an empty result
explainable rather than merely reported.

relaxations.description: Criteria that had to be dropped, as stable keys the UI translates.

track_warnings.description:
What the requested tracks cannot honour (RD-080-02). Warnings, not refusals: a
missing subtitle language must not stop a download that is otherwise right.

variant.description: The variant this selection would store on the candidate.

contract_version.description: [`MEDIA_CONTRACT_VERSION`] of the writer; `0` for a row that predates the selector.

oneOf.description:
The semantic selection, re-resolved before each download.

Boxed because a `MediaSelection` rides inside every `DownloadFile` and every
writer command that carries one; the criteria are consulted once per download, so
paying an indirection there is cheaper than widening the whole queue.

format.description: Extractor format expression, or a streamlink quality for a recording. Kept verbatim.

oneOf.description:
What the last resolve settled on. Advisory: shown in the UI and used to pin a format
id as the expression's first alternative, never trusted on its own.

MediaSelectionRequest.description: A selection to apply, or to preview without applying.

oneOf.description: The full criteria. Wins over `preset`.

preset.description: A preset id (`best`, `1080p`, `audio_mp3`). Ignored when `criteria` is given.

MediaStatusResponse.description: External-tool availability and the hosts routed to the media provider.

apprise.description: The notification CLI; a target may name its own executable, this is the lookup without.

ffprobe.description: yt-dlp needs ffprobe next to ffmpeg to merge streams and convert audio.

vendor_directories.description: Vendor folders searched before `PATH`, in order.

MediaTarget.description: Whether the job wants a video file or audio only.

MediaToolCapabilities.description:
What the tools on this installation allow, so the UI can grey out what cannot work
instead of re-deriving the rule.

can_merge.description: ffmpeg *and* ffprobe are present: separate video and audio streams can be merged.

can_transcode_audio.description: Audio can be extracted and re-encoded.

active_version.description:
The managed version currently activated, if any. Independent of `version`, which is
whatever the resolved binary reports about itself.

compatibility.description: What the compatibility rules make of the version that was found (RD-102-03).

managed.description:
Whether this is a tool the application can manage itself (RD-102-02). A managed tool
may still resolve to a system binary; that is what `source` says.

oneOf.description:
Whether the binary came from the explicit setting, the managed store, a vendor folder
or `PATH`.

MediaVariant.description:
One selectable download option synthesised from the extractor's format list.

This is the *bounded* list that rides along in every LinkGrabber response; the full
inventory is fetched separately, following the [`crate::RemoteListingSummary`] precedent.
Everything after `format` is additive and defaulted, so a blob written before RD-080-01
still deserialises.

abr.description: Audio bitrate in kbit/s when known.

oneOf.description: The criteria this variant stands for; `None` for a legacy row.

requires_merge.description: Whether producing this variant needs ffmpeg to merge two streams.

warnings.description: What this variant cannot honour, if anything.

MessageResponse.description: Action result: English text plus a stable code (and parameters) clients translate.

MfaCredential.description: One enrolled factor. Never carries the secret behind it.

confirmed_at.description:
When the first correct code proved the enrolment works.

An unconfirmed credential does not gate sign-in. Someone who starts enrolling and then
cannot scan the code must not thereby be locked out of their own service.

password.description: The administrator password. Deliberately not a code: a lost phone must not be permanent.

MfaKind.description: What kind of second factor a credential is.

MfaStatus.description: How much of the second factor is set up, for the settings page and the login screen.

enabled.description: Whether at least one confirmed credential exists, so sign-in requires a second step.

recovery_codes_remaining.description:
How many recovery codes are still unspent.

Shown because running out is a problem that only becomes visible at the worst moment.

MirrorPreference.description:
What a person prefers when a mirror group offers a choice (RD-110-19).

Three facets, each optional and each combined with the others by conjunction. It is a
*preference*, not a rule: it decides which member of a group is the chosen one, it never
deletes a mirror and it never overrules a member somebody pinned by hand. Stored on the
server under its own settings key, so it applies to the next package that arrives and to
every package after a restart.

The three are compared case-insensitively against the values [`CandidateMirror`] carries,
which is what the source named or what the release name spells; the hoster is the link's
host without a leading `www.`.

hidden_hosters.description:
Hosters the LinkGrabber hides (RD-130-21), each as [`Self::hoster`] spells one.

Not a fourth facet. A facet narrows the list to what matches it; this takes named
hosters out of it, several at once. Inside a mirror group it only ranks: a member at a
hidden hoster is never the chosen one while a member at a shown hoster exists, and it
stays in the group as the fallback the queue switches to. Stored with the facets because
it is the same kind of standing decision and has to survive a restart the same way.

hoster.description: e.g. `rapidgator.net`. Matched against the link's host.

MirrorSource.description:
Where a mirror group came from (RD-110-18).

Kept beside the group because the three are not equally strong, and the interface has to
be able to say so: a release page that states the five links are one file is a fact, two
links agreeing on name *and* size is evidence, and a bare name in common is a suggestion
somebody may want to overrule.

NetworkInterface.description: One network interface the torrent engine can bind to.

addresses.description: Addresses currently configured on the interface.

loopback.description: Loopback interfaces are listed but never a sensible binding target.

up.description: Whether the interface currently has a usable address.

Note.description: One sentence a person reads, in both forms its two readers need.

code.description: The stable code. The interface translates it under `logs.<code>`.

params.description: Values the sentence interpolates. Data, such as field names, and never translated.

text.description:
The same sentence in English, rendered from the English catalogue with `params`
already interpolated. What the archive carries and what the interface falls back to.

NotificationDestination.description: One installed notification-destination plugin, for the target editor.

name.description: Default display name. The interface prefers the plugin's own localised name.

plugin_id.description: The value a target stores in `config.plugin_id`.

NotificationEvent.description: What happened. Deliberately a closed set: a rule filters on it, so it has to be stable.

NotificationRule.description: Which events of which packages reach which target.

oneOf.description: Restricts the rule to one category; `None` matches all.

NotificationTarget.description: A configured delivery destination. Credentials never live here — only a vault reference.

config.description:
Kind-specific settings without any secret: SMTP TLS mode, sender and recipients,
webhook headers.

endpoint.description:
Webhook: the URL. SMTP: `host:port`. Apprise: the service scheme only, because the
full target URL carries the token and stays in the vault.

has_secret.description: Whether a secret is stored, so the UI can show that without seeing it.

clear_secret.description: Removes the stored secret; an omitted `secret` alone keeps it.

endpoint.description: Webhook: the URL. SMTP: the host. Apprise: the service scheme, for display only.

secret.description:
Webhook signing secret, SMTP password or the full apprise target URL. Write-only:
it goes straight into the vault and is never returned.

NzbFileStatus.description: One NZB file with all persistent segment states.

NzbImport.description: Summary stored after a bounded, entity-free NZB parse.

has_password.description: Whether an archive password (from `{{password}}` in the file name) is stored.

password.description: The stored archive password, in clear; see `DownloadPackage::password` (RD-104-04).

position.description:
Place in the LinkGrabber's manual order, shared with `collector_packages`.

Without it the list cannot render the order it just saved: the two kinds interleave, so a
client that only sees creation times has no way to put an import back where it was
dropped. Deliberately not `#[serde(default)]`: this only ever comes out of the database,
where the column is `NOT NULL`, and a default would make it optional in the generated
contract — leaving every client to invent a fallback position for a value that is always
there.

oneOf.description: Queue priority chosen at import time; `None` = the default at enqueue time.

NzbImportEnqueueRequest.description:
How an NZB import enters the download queue.

The body is optional: a request without one keeps the previous behaviour and starts the
package immediately.

paused.description: Creates every download of the package paused instead of starting it immediately.

NzbImportState.description: Persistent lifecycle of an imported NZB.

NzbImportUpdateRequest.description: Editable routing metadata of an NZB waiting in the LinkGrabber.

NzbSegmentState.description: Crash-recoverable state of one NNTP article.

NzbSegmentStatus.description: Persisted article metadata and its latest verified CRC.

Operator.description: How a field is compared to a value.

PackageBulkRequest.description: Category and/or priority change for several packages.

PackageClearResponse.description: What a clear pass did: whole packages removed, and the ones it refused to touch.

PackageClearScope.description: Which finished packages the "clear the list" action should remove.

PackageClearSkip.description: A package the clear pass deliberately left alone, and the stable code saying why.

name.description: The package name, so the reader can find it without looking up the id.

PackageDeleteRequest.description:
Packages to remove from the download list.

`force` is the difference between tidying up and throwing work away: without it a package
whose files are still running, waiting or seeding is refused, because removing it cancels
those files and deletes what they had already written.

force.description: Cancels running files and removes the package anyway.

PackageFolderRequest.description: New name for a package **and** for the folder its files live in (RD-106-13).

name.description:
New name (1–200 characters), sanitized into a folder name by the same rules a file
rename uses. A folder of that name that already exists is refused, not avoided.

PackageReorderRequest.description: Complete queue order; packages are positioned in the given sequence.

PackageState.description: Lifecycle of a download package as a whole.

PackageUpdateRequest.description: Category and/or priority change for one package.

clear_password.description: Removes the stored archive password when `true`.

password.description:
Archive password used for extraction.

Readable again on the package (RD-104-04); see `DownloadPackage::password`.

oneOf.description: Explicit post-processing level; see `clear_postprocess_level` to inherit again.

script.description: Post-processing script file name inside the scripts directory.

PasskeyChallenge.description: What starting a ceremony hands back.

ceremony_id.description: Echoed back to finish the ceremony. Identifies the challenge, does not authorise it.

options.description:
The `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions` or `…RequestOptions` to hand to the browser.

Opaque here on purpose: this is a W3C-defined structure that the browser parses, and
restating its shape in our own schema would only create a second definition to keep in
step with the first.

label.description:
What to call this passkey in the list. Asked for after the ceremony, so nobody has to
name a key before finding out whether their authenticator would produce one.

PasswordChangeRequest.description:
A change of the administrator password by somebody who knows the current one (RD-120-22).

Both fields are `write_only`: neither may ever appear in a response, and the generated
schema is what keeps a future handler from echoing one back.

current_password.description: The password in force now. Wrong is refused exactly as a wrong sign-in is.

new_password.description: The replacement, judged by the same policy the first password was.

PendingAction.description: A power action waiting out its countdown.

cycle.description: The work cycle this action belongs to; a restart mid-countdown resumes the same one.

PendingCaptcha.description:
A captcha the user is being asked to solve.

Image and click-point challenges carry their picture as a `data:` URI so the UI can show
it without a second request; widget challenges carry only their site key and page, which
is all a solver service needs and all the UI can meaningfully display.

PendingWidget.description:
A widget challenge as the desktop agent needs to see it.

Deliberately narrower than [`PendingCaptcha`]: a capture token is a restricted credential,
and everything an agent needs to open the right page is here — nothing else is. There is
no image, no prompt and, above all, no answer.

page_url.description: The hoster page the WebView must load; the token is only valid for this origin.

PluginDigestRevocationRequest.description:
Which package to withdraw: the digest itself, or the installed version to hash.

Both spellings exist because both questions are real. An operator acting on an advisory has
a digest and may not have the package installed at all; an operator acting on what the
plugin manager shows has an id and a version and no way to compute a digest by hand.

digest.description: The content digest, 64 hex characters. Wins over `plugin_id`/`version` when both are sent.

reason.description: Why, in the operator's own words. Kept verbatim and shown beside the entry.

digest.description: The package's content digest, 64 lowercase hex characters.

plugin_id.description: Which plugin it belonged to, when that was known when it was withdrawn.

PluginExecutionResponse.description: One recorded plugin invocation, as the diagnostics card shows it.

correlation_id.description: Bare UUID a user can quote in a report; it identifies the entry and nothing else.

error_class.description: Stable failure code, when there was one.

message.description: Redacted message; never a credential, a token or a header value.

PluginTrustedKeyResponse.description: One plugin signing key the user confirmed on first use.

fingerprint.description: Hex SHA-256 of the public key, as shown when it was confirmed.

PolicySource.description: Which level supplied one effective value.

PostprocessKind.description: Persistent kind of one postprocessing operation.

PostprocessLevel.description:
Cumulative post-processing level (`Repair` ⊂ `Unpack` ⊂ `Delete`), like SABnzbd's
`+R` / `+RU` / `+RUD` job options.

PostprocessPluginStep.description: One installed post-processing step plugin, for the settings and category editors.

name.description: Default display name. The interface prefers the plugin's own localised name.

plugin_id.description: The value a category or the global list stores.

PostprocessQueueEntry.description: One package currently in (or waiting for) the post-processing pipeline.

pending.description: `true` while the job waits for the single post-processing worker.

PostprocessScriptsResponse.description: Script files available in the configured scripts directory.

PostprocessStage.description: Pipeline stage a package is currently in while post-processing.

PostprocessState.description: Crash-recoverable lifecycle of a postprocessing operation.

PostprocessStatus.description: Live status of a package's post-processing pipeline.

current.description: File or script currently being processed.

percent.description: 0–100 for the current stage when known.

code.description:
Stable code for the outcome this step recorded, translated by the interface.

`message` stays the English text the server produced and remains the fallback for a
code nobody knows; the code is what makes an outcome like "the recovery set is too
small" sayable in four languages instead of only in the server's own words
(RD-107-04). Set on the outcomes that are worth naming, `None` on the rest.

owner_id.description: Owning NZB import or download package id (UUID text).

params.description: Flat parameters interpolated into the translated `code` (counts, names).

position.description: Pipeline order (par2 → unpack → delete → cleanup → script).

progress_percent.description: 0–100 while running, when the step reports progress.

PowerCapabilities.description: What the machine underneath can actually do.

battery.description: Whether battery state can be read at all.

inhibit_display.description: Whether the display can be kept awake as well.

inhibit_standby.description: Whether the machine can be kept awake while work is in flight.

metered.description: Whether the connection can be told to be metered.

PowerState.description: The live power and network context; `None` means "cannot tell on this platform".

approval_missing.description:
Set while a power action is configured but has no local approval, so the UI can say
why nothing will happen.

inhibiting.description: Whether the machine is currently being kept awake.

paused_reason.description: Why the queue is paused by the network context, if it is.

ProviderCredentialsResponse.description:
The shape of the credential(s) a provider account stores (mirrors
`rd_provider_registry::CredentialKind`).

ProviderKindResponse.description:
Whether a provider resolves links for its own domains or other hosters' domains
(mirrors `rd_provider_registry::ProviderKind`).

ProviderResponse.description: One entry of the provider registry, exposed for the accounts settings UI.

cookie_scope_host.description:
The host of the provider's `cookie_scope`, when its plugin declares one: the one site
whose session the browser extension can hand over to an account (RD-120-45).

credential_modes.description:
The credential modes this provider offers, in the order the form should present them.
Empty for every provider with only one way to hold an account.

device_flow.description:
Whether an installed plugin can sign this provider in without a key being typed
(RD-090-13). A run-time fact, not a registry one: it depends on what is installed.

plugin_id.description:
The plugin behind this provider, and the version of it that is in use.

Two versions of one plugin can be installed at once and the highest wins. That is well
defined but was invisible: the dropdown said "DDownload" either way, so nobody could tell
which one an account would actually be served by.

source.description: Whether this provider is compiled in or contributed by an installed plugin.

ProviderSourceResponse.description: Where a provider row came from (mirrors `rd_provider_registry::ProviderSource`).

ProxyProfile.description: User-configured network proxy without plaintext credentials.

QuietWindow.description: One quiet window; local times in the configured timezone.

end_minute.description: Exclusive; below `start_minute` the window wraps past midnight.

ReconnectPhase.description: Where the last attempt got to, so the interface can say what is happening.

ReconnectStatus.description: The reconnect state, as the interface sees it.

blocked_hosts.description: Hosters currently held back by an address limit.

next_allowed_at.description: Earliest time another attempt may run.

RecordNowRequest.description: Immediate one-off recording of a livestream URL.

RecordingPolicy.description: Everything RD-080-09 adds to one recording.

reconnect_delay_seconds.description: Seconds to wait before reconnecting after an unexpected end.

RecordingSegment.description:
One continuous stretch of recording.

A new segment starts when the split policy says so *or* when a disconnect ends the last
one. Both are the same event as far as the files are concerned; only `reason` differs, and
it is kept because "this recording has a gap in it" is something a person needs to know.

index.description: 1-based, matching the number in the file name.

RecordingState.description: The persisted state of one recording (RD-080-09).

reconnects.description: How many times the stream had to be reconnected.

vod_fetched.description: Whether a VOD was fetched to fill in for an incomplete recording.

RemoteCredential.description:
A stored login for one `protocol://host:port` and user.

Secret values live in the secret store; this struct only ever carries opaque
`vault://` references, and those are never serialized.

host.description: Lowercased, IDNA-encoded host without a trailing dot.

passive.description:
FTP data connections use PASV/EPSV; turning this off asks for an active PORT/EPRT
connection instead. Ignored by SFTP and WebDAV.

RemoteCredentialTestResponse.description: Redaction-safe result of a live remote login check.

code.description: Stable failure code when the check did not succeed.

params.description: Parameters belonging to `code`, including an SSH fingerprint awaiting confirmation.

RemoteEntry.description: One file or directory returned by a remote listing.

etag.description: Server-supplied validator (WebDAV `ETag`); `None` for FTP and SFTP.

path.description: Path relative to the listing root, using `/` separators and never starting with one.

RemoteJob.description: One job running at a provider, as the row holds it.

adoption_checked.description:
Whether the provider has already been asked what it holds for this content key.

Separate from the attempt count because it answers a different question: the count says
how often something was created, this says whether the crash window has been looked
into. Asking twice would be harmless and not asking at all would not.

chosen.description: What they answered. Empty until they do; never filled in on their behalf.

code.description: Stable translation code the interface switches on.

content_key.description:
What `identify` answered for the source. Unique per account, and the reason a magnet
submitted twice cannot become two jobs.

entries.description: What the person is being asked, for a job in `AwaitingChoice`.

message.description: Redaction-safe English text, for a job that failed.

oneOf.description: The LinkGrabber package the finished addresses go to, once there is one.

plugin_id.description:
Which plugin runs it. Read from the row rather than guessed: only one plugin claims a
provider in this world, and which one a due row belongs to is not a search.

remote_id.description: The provider's own identifier, written the moment `submit` answers.

submit_attempts.description: How often the provider has been asked to create this job.

RemoteJobChoiceRequest.description: The entries a person picked, by the provider's own identifiers.

entries.description: Entry ids the job offered. Anything else is dropped rather than forwarded.

RemoteJobFile.description: One entry inside a remote job, as a person is shown it.

id.description: The provider's own identifier for the entry. What a choice names.

path.description: Where it sits inside the job, already reduced to a path that cannot leave it.

selected.description: Whether the provider preselected it — a default, not an answer.

RemoteJobSourceKind.description: What kind of thing was handed over. Kept so a restart can re-offer the same source.

RemoteJobState.description:
Where a remote job has got to, in the host's own vocabulary.

Deliberately not the provider's list. Real-Debrid names ten states, Premiumize five and
AllDebrid a different five; what they share is these six, and a plugin's job is to say
which of the six a provider's word means.

RemoteListing.description: What one remote link resolved to.

root.description: Absolute path on the server the entries are relative to.

single_file.description: `true` when the link addressed a single file rather than a directory.

supports_resume.description:
Whether the server offered a resumable transfer (FTP `REST`, HTTP `Accept-Ranges`).
`false` means an interrupted download has to start over, which the UI states.

oneOf.description: Set when a limit stopped the walk; the entries present are still valid.

RemoteListingPlanRequest.description: The file selection of one remote directory candidate.

excluded.description: Paths that are excluded; excluding a directory excludes everything below it.

RemoteListingSummary.description: Listing metadata without the entries themselves.

RemoteProtocol.description: Transfer protocol a credential and a link belong to.

RemuxTarget.description: What the finished recording is converted to.

ReplayBlockReason.description:
Why a captured request cannot be replayed.

Every variant has a translated explanation in the web UI: a capture that cannot be
reproduced must say why, not disappear.

ReplayBodyKind.description:
Body shapes a replay can reproduce safely.

Deliberately excludes `multipart/form-data`: reproducing it means reproducing a file
part, which is out of scope.

ReplayConsent.description: A person's explicit approval of one replay, bound to the template it was given for.

approved_origins.description: Origins the person approved, always a subset of the server-derived set.

template_hash.description: [`stable_hash`] of the template at the moment consent was granted.

ReplayConsentRequest.description: A person's approval of one specific captured request.

approved_origins.description: Origins being approved; must be a subset of the preview's `approved_origins`.

template_hash.description:
`template_hash` from the preview the person actually looked at.

Approving a template that has since changed must fail rather than silently apply to
the new one, so this is required rather than advisory.

ReplayMethod.description: HTTP method a replay may use.

ReplayPreviewResponse.description:
Exactly what a replay of this capture would send, and to where.

This is the payload the consent dialog renders, so it has to be complete enough that a
person can make an informed decision and contain nothing that would be harmful to show.

approved_origins.description: Origins the replay may follow redirects into.

oneOf.description: Body description: kind, size and field *names*. Never values.
Consent already on file, if any.

credential_categories.description: Which categories of credential this replay would send.

effective_url.description: Redacted URL the browser actually ended up at, when it differs.

target_origin.description: Origin the request itself goes to.

template_hash.description: Hash the consent is bound to; the client sends it back when approving.

url.description: Link URL with every signature and credential parameter redacted.

ReplaySummary.description:
What a download row exposes about its replay without carrying the template itself.

`DownloadFile` is serialized into REST responses and SSE payloads, so it gets this
summary while the full template stays behind an explicit database read.

ResolvedFormatPlan.description: The outcome of the last resolve, carried alongside a selection for display and pinning.

format_ids.description: Format ids the last resolve chose, in `-f` order.

relaxations.description: Criteria that had to be dropped to reach this result.

ResolvedRemoteEntry.description: One entry with the selection applied.

ResolvedRemoteListing.description: A listing plus its selection, as handed to the UI and used at enqueue time.

ResolvedTorrentPlan.description: The full resolution result for one torrent.

Run.description: One execution of one automation version against one event.

action_index.description: Index of the action being executed or waiting to be retried.

event_id.description: The event that started it, for display and for the idempotency key.

message.description: Redacted outcome of the last attempt.

oneOf.description: The package the actions operate on; `None` for a trigger that names none.

download_enforced.description: Whether the download limit reaches this transport at all.

note.description: Short reason shown next to an unenforced entry; `None` when fully enforced.

scoped_enforced.description:
Whether the transport can be limited per host, account or category, or only as a
whole. External helper processes only take one rate for the whole job.

SaveSiteRuleRequest.description: Writing one of the person's own rules.

enabled.description:
Whether it is consulted. A rule created from the editor may be on right away; an
imported one may not, and the import endpoint never asks for this.

rule.description: The rule body. Parsed through `rd_siterules::Rule` and validated before it is stored.

oneOf.description: A single known broadcast.

start.description:
The instant it starts, in UTC. A one-off has an absolute time because it refers
to one event, not to a time of day.

oneOf.description: A recurring local time on chosen weekdays.

days.description: ISO weekdays, `1` = Monday through `7` = Sunday. Duplicates are ignored.

oneOf.description: Profile used outside every window; empty = no limits.

timezone.description: IANA timezone the windows and budget periods are read in.

ScheduleWindow.description: One time window that activates a profile.

end_minute.description: Exclusive end; a value below `start_minute` wraps past midnight into the next day.

priority.description: Higher wins where windows overlap; ties go to the later start.

end_minute.description: Exclusive; below `start_minute` the window wraps past midnight.

ScheduledRunState.description: What became of one planned occurrence.

ScopeDescriptor.description:
One area a token can be granted, with what it costs and what it reaches.

Sent to the token editor so the choice is made against real numbers. Everything here is
derived from the same table that enforces the scopes, so the preview cannot drift away
from the behaviour it is previewing.

implies.description: What holding this scope also confers, e.g. `api:read` for anything that acts.

operations.description:
How many API operations a token holding exactly this scope reaches, implications
included.

sensitive.description:
Whether this area carries stored credentials or service administration.

Flagged rather than left to the label: these are the two areas nothing else confers,
and the two whose consequences are worst to grant by accident.

bytes_per_second.description: Download limit in bytes per second for everything in this scope.

ScopeLimit.description: One scope's own limit inside a profile.

oneOf.description: Seed until the ratio target or a manual stop ends it.

SeedTimeLimit.description: How long a finished torrent keeps seeding.

SeedingPolicyOverride.description: A partial seeding policy. Every `None` field inherits from the level above.

ratio_milli.description: Stored as milli-ratio so the override stays `Eq` and round-trips exactly.

SeedingPolicyRequest.description:
A seeding override as the API takes it.

Every field is optional twice over: absent means "inherit", and an explicit `null`
clears a value that was set before. That is the only way to express "stop overriding
this one field" in a single request.

time_minutes.description: Minutes to seed; `null` with `time_unlimited` unset leaves the field inheriting.

time_unlimited.description: Seed without a time limit, overriding an inherited one.

SeedingPolicyResponse.description: The effective policy of one torrent, with the source of every field.

oneOf.description: The override stored on this torrent, if any.

Session.description: One session in the inventory. Never carries the bearer, only what it is for.

client_ip.description: Where the session was created from, as the proxy rules resolved it.

current.description:
Whether this is the session making the request.

Computed per request rather than stored: it is a property of who is asking, not of the
session. It is what lets the interface offer "sign out everywhere else" without the
caller having to work out which row is its own — and what stops that action from
signing the caller out too.

expires_at.description:
When the session ends if it is not used again: the earliest of the expiry fixed at
sign-in and the two limits in force now (see [`SessionLimits::ends_at`]).

user_agent.description: The client's user agent, truncated, or `None` if it sent none.

SetDownloadAuthProfileRequest.description: Which profile a single download uses.

SettingsResponse.description: Mutable local service settings exposed in version one.

admin_login_disabled.description: Switches the administrator login off (only sensible on a trusted loopback/LAN setup).

audit_retention_days.description: Days an audit record is kept at most (30-3650), whatever the count.

audit_retention_records.description:
Audit records the append-only audit log keeps at most (10000-2000000); the oldest
whole records go first (RD-110-03).

auto_remove_delay_hours.description: How long a package stays after it finished, in hours (1–720).

auto_remove_finished.description: Remove finished packages from the queue once they have been finished long enough.

auto_remove_keep_failed.description: Keep a finished package that still holds a file which did not complete.

oneOf.description: Bandwidth profile applied outside every schedule window; empty = no limits.

bandwidth_timezone.description: IANA timezone the bandwidth schedule and its budget periods are read in.

byte_display.description:
How byte counts are rendered in the interface: `binary` (KiB/MiB/GiB, 1024) or
`decimal` (kB/MB/GB, 1000). Purely a display choice — nothing computes with it.

byte_unit.description:
Which magnitude of the ladder byte counts are printed in: `auto` picks the step that
fits each value, while `byte`, `kilo`, `mega`, `giga`, `tera` or `peta` pin every value
to that step so a list of sizes can be compared column by column (RD-106-14).

Named by magnitude rather than by unit because the unit names belong to `byte_display`:
`mega` reads as MiB on the binary ladder and MB on the decimal one.

cleanup_extensions.description: Extensions (without dot) deleted from the package folder after unpacking.

oneOf.description: What runs once the queue and post-processing have drained.

completion_countdown_seconds.description: Seconds a power action counts down before it runs (10–3600).

completion_script.description: Script name inside the post-processing scripts directory.

oneOf.description: When the session cookie is marked `Secure`.
Post-processing level for packages without an explicit or category level.

delete_archives_after_extract.description: Remove archive volumes after a successful extraction.

delete_par2.description:
Delete the PAR2 recovery set once repair and extraction have both succeeded. Off by
default: it is the only thing that can rescue a damaged package.

disabled_plugins.description:
