Plugin ids the user switched off. They stay installed and listed — otherwise they could
not be switched back on — but are not loaded, compiled or executed.

dlc_service_enabled.description:
Import `.dlc` containers. Off by default on purpose: the format cannot be decrypted
locally, so every import sends the container's key to the service below.

dlc_service_endpoint.description: `dlcrypt` service that unwraps the container key; empty = the JDownloader service.

enable_all_par.description:
Download every PAR2 recovery volume of an NZB straight away. Off by default, like
SABnzbd's `enable_all_par`: the main index comes down with the payload, the `vol`
volumes wait, and only a repair that is short of blocks fetches as many of them as the
gap needs (RD-107-04). On restores the older behaviour of fetching all of them.

excluded_domains_file.description:
Absolute path of the domain blocklist (one host per line); empty =
`excluded_domains.txt` next to the database.

external_url.description:
What the outside world calls this service: `https://rd.example.com/downloads`.

Carries the scheme, host and mount point together so they cannot disagree.

gallery_executable.description: Absolute path of gallery-dl; empty = look up in the vendor folders and on PATH.

gallery_hosts.description: Hosts handled by the gallery provider (without `www.`).

hotfolder_poll_seconds.description:
Seconds between two reconciliation scans of every watched folder (RD-110-31); 5 to
3600, one value for all folders, taken over by running watchers without a restart.

ignore_samples.description: Delete sample files after unpacking and skip sample archives.

keep_import_history.description:
Keep NZB import entries and stored .torrent files after the download finishes;
off removes them automatically on completion.

log_retention_days.description: Days a log record is kept at most (1-365), whatever the count.

log_retention_records.description:
Log records the structured log store keeps at most (1000-500000); the oldest go
first (RD-110-02).

managed_tools_enabled.description:
Whether this installation may download, verify and activate tool versions itself
(RD-102-02). Off by default: fetching executables is not something to start unasked.

managed_tools_manifest_url.description:
`https://` URL of the signed tool manifest; empty = only the manifest compiled into
this build, which is the offline-safe default.

max_connections_per_host.description:
Simultaneous connections one host may see across all running transfers; `0` lifts
the limit entirely.

max_retries.description: Retries per file before a retryable failure becomes final (0–100).

media_check_timeout_seconds.description: Timeout of one metadata probe in seconds (5–600).

oneOf.description: Full default selection for new media links; `None` uses `media_default_variant`.

media_default_variant.description: Variant preselected for new media links (`best`, `1080p`, `720p`, `audio_mp3`, …).

media_ffmpeg_executable.description: Absolute path of ffmpeg; empty = look up on PATH.

media_hosts.description: Hosts handled by the media provider (without `www.`).

media_output_template.description: Default output template for media downloads; `None` keeps the plain file name.

media_ytdlp_executable.description: Absolute path of yt-dlp; empty = look up on PATH.

metadata_enrichment_enabled.description:
Whether installed metadata enricher plugins are asked about resolved links
(RD-090-14). Off by default: an enricher reaches a service outside this machine, and
doing that on the strength of having installed a plugin would be a decision nobody
made.

mirror_detection.description: Treat links in a package that point at the same file as alternatives, downloading one.

nntp_connections_per_file.description:
NNTP connections one NZB file may hold at once; `0` is as many as the enabled
servers allow. A value below the servers' total caps the file (RD-108-25).

otlp_enabled.description:
Whether finished spans are exported over OTLP (RD-110-03). Off by default and off
after an upgrade: exporting traces sends the shape of a person's activity to a third
system, which is a decision somebody takes rather than one they discover.

otlp_endpoint.description:
The collector's OTLP/HTTP traces endpoint, such as
`http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces`. Empty means unconfigured, which is the same as off.

otlp_timeout_seconds.description: How long one export attempt may take before it is abandoned (1-60).

passwords_file.description: Absolute path of the password list (one per line); empty = `passwords.txt` next to the database.

pause_during_postprocess.description: Hold new downloads while a package is post-processing.

pause_on_battery.description: Hold the queue while the machine runs on battery.

pause_on_metered.description: Hold the queue while the connection reports itself as metered.

plugin_steps.description:
Post-processing plugin steps enabled by default, by plugin id and in the order they
run. A category may override the list, including with an empty one.

power_actions_allowed.description: Local approval for standby and shutdown; without it they are never executed.

prevent_display_standby.description: Keep the display awake too, for a machine somebody watches.

prevent_standby.description: Keep the machine awake while downloads or post-processing are actually running.

oneOf.description: Weekly windows during which resource-intensive work waits.

quiet_hours_defer_notifications.description: Group notification deliveries until the quiet period ends.

quiet_hours_defer_postprocess.description: Hold back PAR2 repair, unpacking and uploads during quiet hours.

rclone_executable.description: Absolute path of rclone; empty = look up in the vendor folders and on PATH.

reconnect_abort_active.description: Allow a reconnect while transfers are running; they are paused and resumed around it.

reconnect_enabled.description: Run the reconnect script when free downloads are stuck behind an IP limit.

reconnect_ip_check_urls.description: Addresses asked what the public address is; empty uses the built-in list.

reconnect_min_interval_minutes.description: Shortest gap between two reconnects, in minutes (1–1440).

reconnect_script.description: Script name inside the post-processing scripts directory.

reconnect_timeout_seconds.description: How long a reconnect may take before it is given up on, in seconds (30–900).

reconnect_windows.description:
Weekly windows a reconnect may run in; empty means any time.

The element type is shared with quiet hours, which is the same shape — a weekday set
and a span of local minutes — and lets the interface reuse the same editor.

record_default_quality.description: Stream selection used when a channel has none (`best`, `1080p`, …).

record_max_parallel.description: Concurrent recordings (1–8); recordings never block regular downloads.

record_poll_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between liveness probes of enabled channels (60–3600).

record_streamlink_executable.description:
Absolute path of streamlink; empty = vendor folders (incl. `vendor/streamlink/bin`)
and PATH.

recursive_unpack.description: Also extract archives found inside extracted archives (depth-capped).

remote_ssh_auto_trust.description: Whether an unknown SSH host key may be trusted on first use without asking.

remote_timeout_seconds.description: Connect, login and per-read timeout for FTP/SFTP in seconds (5–600).

safe_postproc.description:
Whether a failed PAR2/SFV/RAR verification blocks unpacking and everything after it.
On by default, like SABnzbd's `safe_postproc`; off means the unpack runs anyway and a
broken recovery set beside intact archives no longer locks a package (RD-104-04).

oneOf.description: Files containing "sample" in their name count as samples only below this size.

script_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds after which a post-processing script is killed (10–86400).

scripts_directory.description: Absolute scripts directory; empty = `scripts` next to the database.

session_idle_hours.description: Hours without a request after which a sign-in ends (RD-130-09); 1 to 720.

session_max_hours.description:
Hours from sign-in after which a session ends however busy it is; 1 to 2160.

A shorter value ends the sessions already past it at once; a longer one applies from
the next sign-in, because the browser keeps the cookie only as long as it was told.

sfv_verify.description: Verify the CRC32 checksums of any `.sfv` index in the package before unpacking.

stats_hourly_days.description:
Days the transfer statistics keep hourly buckets before folding them into daily ones
(RD-110-01); 1 to the retention.

stats_retention_days.description:
Days the transfer statistics are kept at all (RD-110-01); 7 to 3650. The all-time
totals behind the metrics counters are never thinned.

storage_auto_resume.description: Release a blocked storage root by itself once space is free again.

oneOf.description: Free space that must remain on a storage root without an own threshold.

storage_unknown_size_headroom.description: A transfer of unknown size may start while `threshold × factor` bytes are free (1–64).

subscription_item_images_enabled.description:
Show the cover images an indexer announces for its hits (RD-101-17).

On by default, unlike the enricher switch next to it, because nothing is fetched on
the strength of it: the addresses arrive with the search answer the subscription
already makes, and only the browser loads the pictures, lazily. It is still a switch
because loading them tells the indexer which hits are on somebody's screen, and the
details themselves stay visible when it is off.

title_status_enabled.description:
Whether the browser tab reports what is running — the queue rate and the number of
active transfers — instead of the application name alone (RD-106-07).

On by default: a tab that says nothing is what every earlier version had, and the point
of the feature is not having to bring the window forward. It is a switch because a title
that keeps changing is a distraction for some people, and that is not arguable.

tool_compatibility_overrides.description:
Tools whose compatibility verdict is reported but not enforced (RD-102-03). The
warning stays; only the block is dropped, and every skipped block is logged.

torrent_announce_port.description: Port announced to trackers when a mapping uses a different external port.

torrent_bind_interface.description: Network interface every torrent socket binds to; `None` binds to all.

torrent_ip_blocklist_url.description: HTTP(S) URL of an IP blocklist the torrent engine loads at startup.

torrent_kill_switch_enabled.description: Pause torrent traffic when the bound interface disappears.

torrent_listen_port.description: Incoming BitTorrent peer port; empty = a random port. Applied on the next start.

torrent_peer_addresses_visible.description: Show full peer addresses in the torrent peer list instead of the network prefix.

oneOf.description: SOCKS5 proxy profile for outgoing torrent peer connections.

torrent_seed_ratio.description: Seed until uploaded/downloaded reaches this ratio (0 disables the ratio stop).

torrent_seed_time_minutes.description: Stop seeding after this many minutes; empty = no time limit.

torrent_seeding_enabled.description: Seed finished torrents; off completes them immediately after the download.

torrent_service_enabled.description:
Transfer services switched off entirely. A disabled service refuses new links at
intake and blocks whatever it already had queued, with a reason.

Every one defaults to on except nothing: switching a service off is an explicit act.
Torrent is the one that also shares data, which is why it has its own switch for that
rather than being covered by this one.

torrent_sharing_enabled.description:
Upload data to peers at all. **Off by default**, so a fresh installation shares
nothing. Distinct from seeding, which only covers the phase after a download
finishes: the engine uploads while downloading too, and this is what stops it.

oneOf.description: Global torrent upload limit in bytes per second; empty = unlimited. Next start.

torrent_upnp_enabled.description: Ask the router to forward the listen port via UPnP.

trusted_proxies.description:
Address ranges whose `X-Forwarded-For` is believed, as CIDR or bare addresses.

Empty means no header is read and the peer address is the client, which is the safe
default: without it, anyone could name any client they liked.

ui_port.description:
Port the web UI listens on; applied on the next start. `--listen`/`RDOWNLOADER_LISTEN`
override it.

upload_enabled.description: Upload finished packages to an rclone remote as the last post-processing step.

upload_mode.description: `copy` keeps the local files, `move` removes them after a successful upload.

upload_remote.description: rclone target in `remote:path` form; the package folder is created below it.

vendor_directory.description:
Absolute directory searched for yt-dlp/ffmpeg/ffprobe/unrar/7z before `PATH`; empty =
the built-in `vendor` folders next to the executable and in the data directory.

SetupStatus.description: First-run wizard progress plus what the install already has configured.

ephemeral_storage_roots.description: Of those, how many sit on a path that a container restart wipes.

suggested_storage_path.description:
The service's own download directory, offered as the first storage root.

The form used to start on a hardcoded `/downloads`, which is right inside the container
image and wrong on every native install — on Linux the filesystem root belongs to another
user, so accepting the suggestion produced a failure. Suggesting the directory the service
actually writes to means the offered value is one it has already created.

wizard_completed.description: Explicit completion flag, or a storage root already exists.

Severity.description: How serious an event is; a rule can require a minimum.

file_name.description: File name beside the recording, when one was written.

SidecarPolicy.description: Sidecars to capture beside the recording.

chat.description:
Live chat. Requires a provider-specific client, which is why it can be *asked* for and
still be reported unavailable.

metadata.description: The stream's metadata as the provider reported it, written as JSON.

subtitles.description: Subtitles, where the provider carries them as a separate track.

thumbnail.description: The channel's thumbnail, where the provider names one.

SidecarStatus.description:
Why a requested sidecar was not produced.

Recorded rather than silently dropped: "I asked for chat and there is none" has to be
distinguishable from "the recording forgot".

SignedSiteRuleFile.description:
The signed rule file every release carries (RD-130-07): an `rd_sign` envelope over a
rule pack.

Described here for the contract only. The import reads the request's bytes itself,
because the signature covers the payload exactly as it arrived and a parsed and
re-serialised copy would no longer be what was signed.

payload.description: The rule pack as signed: `format_version`, `sequence`, `issued_at` and `rules`.

SiteRuleCheckResponse.description: What the last self-test said about one rule (RD-110-09).

code.description: The refusal's stable code, absent exactly when the rule answered.

SiteRuleDocument.description:
The exchange format of the export and the unsigned import: the person's own rules and
nothing else.

Deliberately not a `RulePack`: a pack is a signed document under its own trust root, and a
file somebody was sent is not one. Calling it a pack would invite the two to be confused
at exactly the boundary where the difference matters -- which is why the import tells the
two apart by the envelope, never by what the payload claims (RD-130-07).

format_version.description: The rule format these bodies are written in; `1` is what this build reads.

rules.description: The rule bodies, as `rd_siterules::Rule` serialises them.

SiteRuleFileSignature.description: One signature of a [`SignedSiteRuleFile`], as `rd_sign::DocumentSignature` writes it.

key_id.description: The trusted key the signature claims, `rdownloader-siterules-v1` for the project's file.

SiteRuleGroupResponse.description: One group, with its own switch.

rules.description: How many rules carry this group.

SiteRuleImportRequest.description:
What the import accepts: the signed file of a release, or an export of somebody's own
rules. A body carrying `signatures` is read as the first and nothing else.

SiteRuleResponse.description: One rule as the list shows it.

active.description: Whether the rule is actually consulted: its own switch **and** its group's.

enabled.description: The switch on the rule itself.

hosts.description: The hosts the rule claims, `match.hosts` verbatim.

rule.description: The rule body, as `rd_siterules::Rule` serialises it, so the editor can open it.

steps.description: How many steps the rule takes, for the row.

SiteRuleSwitchRequest.description: Switching one rule or one group.

SiteRulesResponse.description: The whole list, ordered by group and then by name.

SolveCaptchaRequest.description: The answer to one waiting captcha.

oneOf.description:
One file, however long it runs. A disconnect still starts a new segment — that is
recovery, not splitting.
Cut after this many minutes.
Cut after this many mebibytes.

SplitPolicy.description: How a long recording is cut up.

categories.description:
Categories to act on; empty with an active mode means `sponsor` only, never "all" —
a mode toggle should not silently start cutting intros as well.

SponsorCategory.description:
A SponsorBlock segment category. A closed set: these are the identifiers the public API
defines, and anything else would be passed to yt-dlp unvalidated.

SponsorMode.description: What to do with the segments SponsorBlock reports.

SshHostKey.description: A server host key the user confirmed once, so a later change is visible as a change.

algorithm.description: Key algorithm as SSH names it (`ssh-ed25519`, `rsa-sha2-512`, …).

fingerprint.description: `SHA256:<base64>` exactly as OpenSSH prints it, so it can be compared by eye.

StatsBucketWidth.description:
The width of the buckets a response is folded to; `rd_db::StatsResolution` as the
contract names it, kept apart because the store crate carries no OpenAPI schema.

StatsRange.description: How far back the statistics reach.

minimum_free_bytes.description: Effective threshold: the root's own value, else the global default.

oneOf.description: `None` for the service download directory, which is not a configured root.

target.description: Path segment for the resume action.

StoragePersistence.description: Whether writes below a storage root outlive the container.

StorageRootConfig.description: Allowlisted filesystem root available to categories.

oneOf.description:
Free space that must remain on this root after a download finishes; `None`
inherits `storage_minimum_free_bytes` from the service settings.

StorageRootResponse.description:
A storage root plus the runtime verdict on its path.

Deliberately not a field on `rd_core::StorageRootConfig`: that type is also the backup
type, and a machine-local verdict written into an exported bundle would mean nothing on
the machine that restores it.

StorageSpace.description: Free and total capacity of one storage root.

oneOf.description: `None` when the path is currently unreachable.

StreamChannel.description: A channel watched by the monitor; recordings start automatically while it is live.

oneOf.description: Destination category of recordings; `None` = the default category.

last_error.description: Last probe error, cleared on a successful probe.

name.description: Display name; doubles as the recording file prefix.

recording.description:
Splitting, remux, sidecars and VOD fallback for this channel's recordings
(RD-080-09).

url.description: Channel page URL handed to streamlink.

StreamChannelRequest.description: Editable fields of a monitored livestream channel.

name.description: Display name; defaults to the URL host. Doubles as the recording file prefix.

quality.description: streamlink stream selection (`best`, `1080p`, …); `null` = the default quality.

recording.description: Splitting, remux, sidecars and VOD fallback for this channel (RD-080-09).

lead_minutes.description: Extra minutes of watching before the window, for a broadcast that starts early.

replay_from_start.description:
Ask the provider to start from the beginning of the stream, where it can.

Only ever honoured when the provider actually offers it; see
[`StreamScheduledRun::replay_used`].

timezone.description:
IANA zone the local time is interpreted in, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`. Never an offset:
an offset does not survive daylight saving.

trail_minutes.description: Extra minutes after it, for one that overruns.

window_minutes.description: How long the window lasts, from its nominal start.

StreamSchedule.description: A planned recording of one channel.

timezone.description:
IANA zone, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`. An offset is refused: it does not survive daylight
saving, which is the entire reason this field is not a number.

StreamScheduledRun.description:
One occurrence of a schedule.

Rows are created ahead of time rather than at the moment they fire, so a missed window is
visible as a row that ended in [`ScheduledRunState::Missed`] instead of being invisible
by never having existed.

oneOf.description: The recording this run started, once it has one.

replay_used.description:
Whether replay-from-start was actually available and used, as opposed to merely
asked for. Recorded so the UI never claims a capability the provider did not offer.

starts_at.description: The nominal start, which is also the idempotency key together with the schedule.

SubmitRemoteJobRequest.description:
A source handed to one account's provider.

Exactly one of the three fields is given. They are separate fields rather than one tagged
value because they are different things and the provider treats them differently: a
magnet names content, a plain address names a place, a container is the file itself. A
request carrying more than one, or none, is refused under `remote_job.source_invalid`
rather than resolved by a rule the caller would have to know.

address.description: A plain `http(s)` address the provider fetches for itself (RD-120-20).

container.description:
A `.torrent` or `.nzb` file, base64 with the standard alphabet, at most 16 MiB once
decoded (RD-120-31). The plugin reads the format from the bytes.

SubmitRemoteJobResponse.description: What handing a source over produced.

already_running.description:
True when the account already had a job for this content. Nothing was written and
nothing was sent — this is the duplicate guard answering, not a failure.

autoplay.description:
Whether the card slider turns its pages on its own (RD-120-37). Off by default, and
meaningless for the list; the interface pauses it whenever the person is using it.

card_ratio.description: The shape of a card's image area in the card view (RD-120-42); `2:1` by default.

oneOf.description: Destination category of accepted items; `None` = the default category.

category_map.description:
Indexer categories routed to categories of ours (RD-080-11). Empty means every item
lands in `category_id`.

consecutive_failures.description: Consecutive failed polls, which is what the backoff is computed from.

etag.description: Feed caching (RD-080-10); ignored by the other kinds.

every_release.description:
Keep every release of an episode rather than only the first (RD-110-21).

The default is `false`, which is the whole point of a release-page subscription: the
same episode is posted again in another group's release, another quality and another
week, and without this being off a subscription enqueues it every time. `true` is the
explicit counter-choice for somebody who collects versions.

has_secret.description: Whether a key is stored, which is all a client is told about it.

last_error.description: Last poll error, cleared by a successful poll. Redacted before it is stored.

next_run_at.description: When the scheduler intends to poll next; also what a backoff pushes out.

primed.description: Whether the first poll has happened. Until it has, the backlog policy applies.

schedule.description:
A cron expression (five fields, the service's local time) that replaces the interval
when set (RD-130-19). Only a script subscription carries one.

source_categories.description:
The indexer categories to ask for, sent as `cat`. Empty means "everything", which is
what every subscription written before this field did.

Deliberately not derived from `category_map`: the two answer different questions. One
can want a category fetched without redirecting it anywhere — it lands in the default —
and one can keep a mapping for a category one is not fetching at the moment. Folding
them together would make each choice change the other.

view.description: How the LinkGrabber draws this subscription's pending hits (RD-120-37).

SubscriptionBulkStateResponse.description: Result of setting every item that was pending when a bulk action started.

SubscriptionCardRatio.description:
The shape of a card's image area in the card view (RD-120-42).

Chosen per subscription because the pictures differ per source: a music search brings
square covers, a series search wide banners. `2:1` is the default because it is closest to
the fixed height every card had before the choice existed. The spelling on the wire and in
the store is the ratio itself, so a reader never has to translate a name back into numbers.

SubscriptionFilters.description:
Filters applied to a discovered item, in the order the UI lists them.

Every field is optional and an empty one means "no opinion", so a filter set written by
an older version still deserialises and still means the same thing.

languages.description:
Accepted language tags, compared case-insensitively on the primary subtag so `en`
matches `en-GB`.

min_height.description: Minimum vertical resolution, where the source reports one.

published_after.description: Rejects items published before this instant, independently of the backlog policy.

title_contains.description: Case-insensitive substrings; an item must contain at least one when non-empty.

title_excludes.description:
Case-insensitive substrings; an item containing any of them is rejected. Applied
after `title_contains`, so an exclusion always wins.

SubscriptionHistoryClearResponse.description: Rows removed by a per-subscription history cleanup.

SubscriptionItem.description:
One item a poll found.

The row exists whatever the outcome — accepted, filtered or skipped as backlog — because
its presence is what stops the next poll from looking at it again. A skipped item that
were simply not stored would be rediscovered forever.

attributes.description:
What the source said *about* the release (RD-101-17): cover address, ids, resolution,
size, and whatever else the indexer chose to emit.

Already filtered by `rd_subscription::retain_attributes` before it was stored, so a
value here is safe to render; the `password` key is the specification's flag
(`1` protected), never the secret itself.

item_key.description: Canonical, source-stable identity. Unique per subscription.

media_type.description:
The media type the source declared for `url`, when it declared one.

What an indexer hands over is not visible in its download address, so this is what
decides whether the link is imported as an NZB or a torrent rather than fetched as an
ordinary file.

password.description:
The archive password the source announced, when it announced one.

Deliberately readable like `DownloadPackage::password`: release passwords come from the
title, feed or NZB rather than from an account credential, and seeing the exact value is
what lets a person diagnose an extraction failure. The subscription routes still require
an authenticated session.

oneOf.description: Which rule rejected it, when one did.

source_category.description:
The category the source assigned, kept raw so a mapping added later still applies to
items that were archived before it existed.

SubscriptionItemCounts.description: Counts of every item state in one subscription, independent of the selected page filter.

SubscriptionItemPage.description: One server-filtered page of a subscription's item archive.

counts.description: State totals across the entire subscription, not just this page.

run_total.description: Number of recorded checks that the history cleanup would remove.

total.description: Number of rows matching the selected state filter.

SubscriptionItemState.description: What happened to one discovered item.

SubscriptionKind.description: Where a subscription's items come from.

SubscriptionMode.description: What happens to an item that passes the filters.

api_key.description:
Indexer API key (RD-080-11); write-only, and stored in the vault. Omitting it on an
edit keeps the existing key rather than clearing it.

autoplay.description:
Whether the card slider turns its pages on its own; off unless asked for, and ignored
by the list (RD-120-37).

card_ratio.description:
The shape of a card's image area in the card view: `1:1`, `3:2`, `16:9`, `4:3` or
`2:1` (the default) (RD-120-42). Anything else is refused with
`subscription.card_ratio_unknown` rather than drawn as the default.

category_map.description: Indexer categories routed to categories of ours (RD-080-11).

every_release.description:
Keep every release of an episode rather than only the first (RD-110-21). Only a
watched release page reads it; for every other kind identity is the address anyway.

schedule.description:
A cron expression that replaces the interval: five fields in the service's local time,
e.g. `0 6 * * *` for six every morning (RD-130-19). Only a `script` subscription takes
one; empty or absent keeps the interval.

source_categories.description: Indexer categories to ask for. Empty asks for everything, as before.

view.description:
How the LinkGrabber draws the pending hits: `list` (the default) or `cards`
(RD-120-37).

SubscriptionReviewCount.description: Pending review count for one indexer subscription.

SubscriptionReviewSummary.description: Lightweight indexer-review summary used before any item page is expanded.

SubscriptionRun.description:
One completed poll, kept as history so a silent subscription can be told apart from a
failing one.

accepted.description: Items that were new *and* passed the filters.

error.description: Redacted failure message; `None` for a successful poll.

skipped.description: New items a filter or the backlog cutoff rejected.

SubscriptionView.description:
How the LinkGrabber draws a subscription's hits still waiting for a decision (RD-120-37).

A presentation choice made per subscription rather than once for the application: a music
search reads best as covers to flip through, a series search as the dense list. The list is
the default because it is what every subscription showed before the choice existed.

SubtitleMode.description: What happens to a subtitle track that was asked for.

SubtitlePolicy.description: Which subtitles to fetch and what to do with them.

convert_to.description: Sidecar format to convert to (`srt`, `vtt`, `ass`); `None` keeps what the site serves.

include_automatic.description:
Whether speech-recognition tracks may be used when no manual one exists.

Off by default: an automatic track is a guess, and a guess embedded in a file is
indistinguishable from an authored translation once the file leaves here.

languages.description: Languages to fetch; empty means every manual track the page offers.

SubtitleSource.description: Where a subtitle track came from.

SubtitleTrack.description: One subtitle track a page offers.

formats.description: Formats the track is available in (`vtt`, `srt`, `ttml`), lowercased.

name.description: The site's own name for the track (`English (auto-generated)`).

detail.description: Redacted excerpt of what the target answered; never contains a secret.

TestCaptchaSolverRequest.description:
Credentials to try against the solver service; both fall back to what is stored, so a
key can be checked before it is saved.

api_key.description: Key to test instead of the stored one; never logged and never echoed back.

error.description: Compiler error text when the pattern is invalid.

results.description: One entry per sample in request order; empty when the pattern is invalid.

start.description: First match offsets in UTF-16 code units, ready for JS `String.prototype.slice`.

TestSiteRuleRequest.description: A trial run against a real address, before the rule is saved.

address.description: The address the person named. Must be one the rule claims.

rule.description: The rule body to try. Need not be stored, and is not stored by this call.

address.description:
The address that was actually crawled -- the one given, or the canonical host it was
revived onto when it arrived on a dead domain.

error.description: The run's own refusal, when it produced nothing at all.

kept.description: How many of them would become candidates.

refused.description: How many answered with a page rather than a file and would be dropped.

TestedLinkResponse.description: One address the run produced, with what this installation makes of it.

code.description: The stable code of a refused address, absent when it was kept.

ThirdPartyLicenses.description: The dependency licences, as `scripts/licenses.sh` writes them.

npm.description: Every package of `web/package-lock.json` that npm does not mark as a development one.

rust.description:
Every crate a workspace member depends on as a normal dependency, on any platform —
what ends up in the binaries and the plugin components.

rust_not_shipped.description:
The crates of `Cargo.lock` that only tests and build scripts use, as `name@version`.
They ship nowhere; they are listed so that a crate new to the lockfile can be told
apart from one this list forgot.

license.description:
SPDX expression as the package declares it, or as `licenses/overrides.json` records it
for a package that declares none.

ToolCompatibility.description:
The compatibility verdict for one external tool (RD-102-03).

Four states rather than a boolean, because they call for different answers: `too_old` has
an upgrade, `known_bad` may call for a different version in either direction, and `unknown`
is an absence of information that never blocks anything.

affects.description: What is lost while the verdict is not `supported`. Empty when no rule covers the tool.

min_version.description: The oldest version this build is tested against, when a rule sets one.

overridden.description:
Whether the settings name this tool as overridden, so the verdict is reported but not
enforced.

upgrade.description: One English sentence saying what to do about it, or `null` when there is nothing to do.

version.description:
The version the rules were applied to, normalised when it could be parsed and the raw
line when it could not.

TorrentAggregateStats.description: Aggregate counters of one torrent. Cheap enough to broadcast.

live.description:
Whether these numbers come from a torrent currently in the session. When `false`,
the values are the last known ones and must not be presented as current.

ratio.description: Uploaded divided by total payload size; `0` while nothing has been uploaded.

seeded_seconds.description: Total seconds spent seeding, across restarts.

session_generation.description:
Session incarnation the sample came from. A changed generation tells a client that
the engine was rebuilt and older samples are not comparable.

TorrentCandidateSummary.description:
Bounded summary of a candidate's torrent state.

The full file tree can hold thousands of entries, which would bloat every LinkGrabber
list response. Lists carry this summary; the tree itself is fetched per candidate.

TorrentDetailResponse.description: The torrent view of a link candidate or a queue row.

capabilities.description: What the engine can do, so the UI can disable what it cannot.

metadata_error.description: Redaction-safe reason why metadata resolution failed.

oneOf.description: The resolved file tree; `None` while the metadata is still being fetched.

private.description: Private torrents may not use DHT, PEX or LSD.

web_seeds.description:
BEP 19 web seeds advertised by the torrent, redacted.

Diagnostics only: the engine has no web-seed support, which `capabilities.web_seeds`
reports, so these URLs are shown but never fetched.

engine.description: Name of the engine backing the session.

file_selection.description: Downloading only a subset of the files.

interface_binding.description: Binding all torrent sockets to one network interface.

ip_blocklist_file.description: Loading an IP blocklist from a local file.

ip_blocklist_url.description: Loading an IP blocklist from an HTTP(S) URL.

per_class_proxy.description: Separate proxies for tracker, metadata and peer traffic.

priorities_emulated.description:
Whether priorities are emulated on top of plain include/exclude rather than being
a native engine feature. Emulated tiers are opened one after another, so files in
one tier still download concurrently.

socks5_peer_proxy.description: Routing outgoing peer connections through a SOCKS5 proxy.

tracker_edit.description: Editing the tracker list of an existing torrent.

tracker_proxy.description: Routing tracker announces through the configured proxy.

web_seeds.description:
BEP 19 web seeds as a download source. When `false`, web seeds are still parsed and
shown as diagnostics but never fetched.

TorrentFileDecision.description: The resolved state of one file after applying selection, patterns and priority.

excluded_by_pattern.description: Set when rule 2 excluded the file; carries the pattern that matched.

explicit.description: Whether the user decided this file explicitly (rule 1).

TorrentFilePriority.description: Download priority of a single file. Ordering is meaningful: `High` is the largest.

TorrentListenMode.description: Which peer transports the torrent listener accepts.

TorrentMetadataState.description:
Whether the metadata behind a candidate is known yet. Magnets start out `Pending` and
become `Ready` once the engine has resolved the info dictionary.

TorrentNetworkStatus.description: What the torrent network layer is currently doing.

announce_port.description: Port announced to trackers, when it differs from the listen port.

bound_interface.description: The interface the engine is bound to, if any.

bound_interface_present.description: Whether that interface currently exists and has an address.

kill_switch_engaged.description: Whether the kill switch has paused torrent traffic right now.

kill_switch_window_seconds.description: Seconds within which traffic stops after the interface disappears.

last_rebuild_error.description: Why the last session rebuild failed, if it did. The previous session keeps running.

peer_proxy_configured.description: Whether a SOCKS5 proxy is configured for outgoing peer connections.

peer_proxy_error.description: Why the configured proxy could not be resolved, if it could not.

session_generation.description: The session incarnation the engine is running.

upnp_enabled.description: Whether UPnP port forwarding was requested.

address.description:
Peer address, masked to the network prefix unless the operator opted into full
addresses. Never logged and never persisted.

client.description: Client name advertised in the handshake, when known.

connection.description: Transport of the connection (`tcp`, `utp`), when known.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; `None` on the last page.

total.description: Total number of peers known for this torrent, not just the page.

TorrentPieceAvailability.description:
Bucketed piece availability, so the payload stays constant for a 50-piece torrent and a
50 000-piece one alike.

buckets.description:
Percentage of complete pieces per bucket, 0-100. Never longer than
[`PIECE_BUCKETS`], so the payload does not grow with the torrent.

pieces_per_bucket.description: How many pieces one bucket covers.

TorrentPlanRequest.description:
Replaces the selection of a torrent.

A full replacement rather than a patch: the tree is edited as a whole in the UI, and a
partial update would make the outcome depend on the order of requests.

excluded.description: File indices the user explicitly excluded.

exclusion_patterns.description: Glob patterns excluding files the user has not decided explicitly.

included.description: File indices the user explicitly included.

priorities.description:
Per-file priority tiers. A folder priority is inherited onto its files by the
client, so only per-file entries are ever stored.

oneOf.description: Streaming-oriented piece ordering; rejected unless the engine supports it.

TorrentSequentialMode.description:
Streaming-oriented piece ordering. Only [`TorrentSequentialMode::Off`] is supported by
the embedded engine; the other variants exist so a future engine only has to flip a
capability flag.

label.description: What to call this factor in the list.

TotpEnrolment.description: What enrolment hands back: the thing to scan, and the thing to write down.

recovery_codes.description: Shown once. There is no second chance to read these.

secret.description: The same secret in base32, for an app that cannot scan.

TrackSelection.description: The track side of a media selection (RD-080-02).

oneOf.description: The container cannot hold more than one audio track.
The container cannot hold embedded subtitles.
A requested language is not offered by the page.
Only an automatic track exists for a requested language.
ffmpeg is needed to merge or embed and is not available.

TrackWarning.description: Why a track selection cannot be honoured as asked.

TrackerEntryRequest.description: One tracker in a replacement request.

id.description:
Id of an existing tracker to keep. Set this instead of `url` to keep an entry whose
URL the client never sees in full.

url.description: A new announce URL to add.

trackers.description:
Announce URLs in the order they should be tried. The list is authoritative: an
entry missing from it is removed.

TrackerListResponse.description: The tracker list of one torrent.

editable.description: Whether the engine can act on tracker edits at all.

TrackerOrigin.description: Where a tracker entry came from.

TrackerScrape.description: Cached scrape counters of one tracker.

TrackerView.description: One tracker as the API exposes it.

id.description: Stable id derived from the URL; safe to expose and used to address the entry.

last_error.description: Redaction-safe reason of the last failure.

scrape_stale.description:
Whether the scrape counters are older than the freshness window. Stale counters are
still returned, but never presented as current.

url.description:
The announce URL with userinfo, passkey parameters and passkey path segments
replaced. The full URL never leaves the service.

start.description: Start of the bucket, RFC 3339 in UTC.

TransferStatsBucket.description: One bucket of the range, summed over every kind and provider.

TransferStatsFigures.description: The five figures every row of the statistics carries.

seconds.description: Seconds from creation to completion, summed over the completed transfers.

TransferStatsGroup.description: The range's figures for one kind or one provider.

all_time.description: Everything ever recorded, untouched by the retention.

Trigger.description:
What starts an automation.

A closed set rather than "any event": every variant is one thing a person would describe
as a moment in a download's life, and each one has a contract test. The domain event bus
carries more than this — configuration changes, captcha prompts, tracker statistics — and
none of it is something to hang an action off.

TrustSshHostKeyRequest.description:
Confirms one SSH host key as trusted.

The fingerprint is required rather than implied: confirming "whatever the server offers
next" would make the trust store meaningless, so the caller has to name the key it saw.

fingerprint.description: `SHA256:<base64>`, exactly as reported by the failure that blocked the transfer.

UpdateAccountRequest.description: Editable account metadata. Empty secret fields preserve their stored values.

oneOf.description:
Which credential `secret` holds, for a provider that offers a choice. Required for
those providers, rejected for every other one.

UpdateAuthProfileRequest.description: Editable profile fields. Empty credential fields preserve their stored values.

UpdateCaptchaConfigRequest.description: Partial update of the solver configuration.

api_key.description: New API key; stored in the secret store, never echoed back.

UpdateRemoteCredentialRequest.description: Editable login fields. Empty credential fields preserve their stored values.

clear_private_key.description: Drops the stored private key instead of keeping it.

UpdateUsenetServerRequest.description: Editable NNTP endpoint. An omitted password preserves the stored password.

UploadDestination.description: One installed upload destination plugin, for the post-processing settings.

plugin_id.description: The prefix an upload target uses: `plugin:<plugin_id>/<destination>`.

Verdict.description: What a rule says about the version that was found.

VideoCodecFamily.description: Video codec reduced to the family a person actually chooses by.

oneOf.description:
Never. The default, because fetching a VOD doubles the traffic and the recording is
usually fine.

Fetch the VOD when the live recording covered less than this percentage of the
scheduled window.

value.description:
Fetch the VOD when the live recording covered less than this percentage of the
scheduled window.

VodFallback.description: When an incomplete live recording may be replaced by the published VOD.
